topic: Tata 12V Battery Jump Lead Starting Safety
guide: Jump Lead Starting Use only a battery of same rating & ca- pacity to jump start your vehicle. Position the booster battery close to your vehicle so that the jump leads will reach both batteries. When using a battery of another vehicle, do not let the vehicles touch. Apply the parking brake firmly and keep the gearshift lever in neutral. Turn off all vehicle accessories, except those necessary for safety like hazard warning lamps. Make jump lead connections as follows: Connect one end of the first jump lead to the positive (+) terminal of the discharged battery. Connect the other end to the positive (+) terminal of the booster battery. Connect one end of the second jump lead to the negative ( ) terminal of the booster battery. Make the final connection (other end of the negative terminal) to an un- painted, heavy metal part (i.e. engine mounting stud/nut) of the vehicle of discharged battery. Start the engine of the vehicle with the discharged battery. Before disconnecting the jumper ca- bles, let the engine run for several minutes. If the booster battery you are using is fitted to another vehicle, start the en- gine of the vehicle with the booster battery. Run the engine at moderate speed. Remove the jump leads in the exact reverse order in which you connected them. NOTE Do not disconnect the discharged battery from the vehicle. WARNING Never tow your vehicle with the front wheels on the ground or four wheels on the ground (for- ward or backward), as this may cause serious damage to the transmission. guide: Inflation Check for inflation and condition of your vehicle tyres periodically. Check the pressure in the tyres when they are cold. Keeping the tyres properly inflated gives you the best combination of riding com- fort, handling, tyre life and better fuel ef- ficiency. Over inflation of tyres makes the vehicle ride bumpy and harsh. Tyres are more prone to uneven wear and damage from road hazards. Under inflated tyres reduce your comfort in vehicle handling and are prone to fail- ures due to high temperature. They also cause uneven wear and more fuel con- sumption. NOTE Every time you check inflation pressure, you should also examine tyres for uneven wear, damage and trapping of foreign objects in the treads and wear. topic: Squealing or Grinding Brakes Troubleshooting & Repair
guide: Repair Tip for Squealing or Grinding Brakes: 1. High-pitched squeal when braking usually indicates the brake pad wear indicator clip is touching the rotor (approx 2-3mm pad lining left). Replace brake pads promptly. 2. Metal grinding noise means pads are completely worn down and metal backing plate is contacting rotor; stop driving immediately to avoid rotor damage. 3. Squeak in morning during high humidity is harmless surface rust being scraped off after 2-3 stops. 4. Inspection: Remove wheel, look through caliper inspection hole. Pad thickness must exceed 3.0 mm. Use DOT-4 brake fluid when servicing.

topic: Engine Overheating in Traffic or Highway Emergency Action
guide: Repair Tip for Engine Overheating: 1. If coolant temp exceeds 100°C or warning light turns ON, turn OFF the Air Conditioner immediately and turn ON the cabin heater to maximum fan speed. This pulls heat away from the engine block into the heater core. 2. Pull over safely to the shoulder, put in Neutral/Park, and let engine idle for 1-2 minutes before shutting off so coolant continues circulating. 3. NEVER open the radiator or expansion tank cap while the engine is hot. Wait at least 20-30 minutes until pressure subsides. 4. Check for leaking radiator hoses or broken fan belt. If coolant level is low, refill with 50/50 ethylene glycol coolant or clean water in an emergency.

topic: Rough Idling or Engine Misfire Diagnosis & Spark Plugs
guide: Repair Tip for Rough Engine Idling or Misfires: 1. Common symptoms: Shaking steering wheel at idle, hesitating during acceleration, check engine light blinking (DTC P0300-P0303). 2. Check spark plugs: Recommended replacement every 30,000 to 40,000 km. Inspect electrode tip for black carbon buildup (rich mix) or wet fuel fouling. Electrode gap should be 0.8–0.9 mm. 3. Ignition Coils: Ensure coil pack connectors are tightly clipped. Swap coil between cylinders to see if misfire code follows the coil. 4. Throttle Body: Clean carbon deposits around throttle butterfly valve with aerosol throttle body cleaner spray.

topic: Car Won't Crank or Start Diagnostic Tree
guide: Repair Tip when Vehicle Does Not Crank or Start: 1. Rapid clicking sound when turning key: 12V battery is drained below 10.5V. Terminal clamps may have white sulfate oxidation; clean with wire brush and baking soda paste. 2. Completely silent / dashboard dark: Blown main starter fuse (check 40A/60A engine fuse) or loose negative battery ground wire attached to chassis. 3. Engine cranks rapidly but won't fire: Fuel pump not priming (listen for 2-second hum behind rear seat when ignition is ON) or immobilizer key fob battery is dead. 4. Key Fob Battery Dead: Hold key fob directly against Start/Stop button while pressing clutch/brake to activate RFID backup coil.

topic: Air Conditioning Blowing Warm Air Troubleshooting
guide: Repair Tip for AC Blowing Warm Air: 1. Check AC Compressor Clutch: Look under bonnet with engine idling and AC ON. Verify the center hub of the AC compressor pulley is spinning, not just the outer ring. 2. Cabin Air Filter: Located behind the glovebox. If clogged with dust and leaves, airflow drops dramatically. Replace cabin filter every 15,000 km or 1 year. 3. Condenser Fins: Inspect front grille condenser radiator for bugs/mud clogging air passage; wash with low-pressure water hose. 4. Low R134a/R1234yf refrigerant gas: If compressor short-cycles every 3-5 seconds, refrigerant is low due to an O-ring leak; needs manifold gauge pressure test.

topic: Steering Wheel Vibration & Pulling Inspection
guide: Repair Tip for Steering Wheel Vibration or Pulling: 1. Vibration felt at 80–110 km/h: Front wheel dynamic imbalance. Wheel weights have fallen off or rims have slight bend. Requires dynamic wheel balancing on shop balancer. 2. Vibration felt during braking only: Warped front brake disc rotors caused by excessive heat or uneven caliper guide pin sliding. Rotors must be resurfaced or replaced. 3. Car pulls to left or right when driving straight on flat road: Front wheel alignment (toe-in / camber) is off, or front tyre pressure is unequal (e.g. 26 psi left vs 33 psi right).

topic: Dead Key Fob Battery Emergency Start & Replacement
guide: Repair Tip for Dead Smart Key Fob: 1. If key fob battery dies, slide release catch on back of fob to pull out mechanical emergency key. Insert key into driver door lock cylinder to unlock manually. 2. To start engine with dead fob: Depress brake/clutch pedal, take the smart key fob, and press the Start/Stop button directly using the top end of the key fob. The passive RFID transponder inside the fob will energize through magnetic induction. 3. Battery Replacement: Pry open key fob shell with a coin. Replace old coin cell with a fresh CR2032 3V lithium battery, positive (+) side facing up.

topic: Windshield Wiper Smearing & Blade Replacement
guide: Repair Tip for Wiper Blade Smearing: 1. Streaking or chattering wipers: Clean rubber squeegee blade with a microfiber cloth dipped in rubbing alcohol or washer fluid to remove road grease and sap. 2. Blade Replacement: Lift wiper arm away from glass, press the small plastic release tab on the J-hook, and slide blade down toward bonnet to detach. Slide new 24-inch driver / 16-inch passenger blade on until audible click. 3. Washer Nozzle Clogged: Use a thin sewing pin or needle to unblock the nozzle hole on cowl panel and adjust spray angle.

topic: Case Study 5: Driving Range Reduction Diagnosis
guide: Driving range reduction causes: 1) Under-inflated tyres (dropping below 30 psi increases rolling resistance by 4-6%). 2) High-RPM accelerations and aggressive overtaking in low gears. 3) Continuous AC operation in dense traffic. 4) Clogged engine air filter or fuel injector deposits causing sub-optimal stoichiometric combustion.

topic: Case Study 5: Telemetry Anomaly & Fuel Efficiency Drop Analysis
guide: In sample_drive.csv telemetry, the highest fuel burn occurred during rapid acceleration transitions where RPM reached 3304 RPM at 98 km/h, spiking instantaneous fuel consumption to 11.4 L/100 km compared to 5.8 L/100 km during 65 km/h steady cruise.

topic: Case Study 5: ADAS Disengagement Protocol & Diagnostics
guide: ADAS disengagement sequence: Optical camera vision blocked by heavy monsoon spray or low sun glare causes automatic disengagement of Lane Keep Assist (LKA) and Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC), issuing an audible chime and amber cluster icon while returning lateral steering control to the driver.

topic: Case Study 5: Battery Overheat Pre-Event Analysis
guide: Before battery overheat warning: Engine compartment temperature elevates to 41°C, coolant reaches 93.3°C, and alternator floats at 14.34V under heavy electrical load (FATC max blower + headlights + defogger), gradually elevating battery internal temperature past 58°C triggering DTC P0A7F.

topic: Case Study 5: City vs Highway Energy Consumption Comparison
guide: City driving consumption is 7.8-8.5 L/100 km (12.2 km/L) due to frequent braking, start-stop cycles, and lower gear ratios. Highway cruising in 5th/6th gear at 75-85 km/h consumes 5.6-6.2 L/100 km (16.9 km/L), saving over 28% energy through optimal thermal efficiency and steady momentum.
